context_requirements: Functional expression of calcium-activated potassium channels mediating the slow afterhyperpolarization (SK/KCa2 or related channels)
An excitable or neuroendocrine cellular context in which afterhyperpolarization current is physiologically relevant
None of the nine profiled lines are neuronal or excitable cells; they are melanoma, lung, liver, colon, breast, prostate and immortalized epithelial lines
falsifiers: A reproducible, dose-dependent transcriptional signature at 6 h or 24 h in any of the nine lines that is shared across multiple slow-afterhyperpolarization channel blockers
Enrichment of a specific gene set (e.g., immediate-early genes, ion-channel or calcium-signaling genes) that distinguishes this class from unrelated drugs
Evidence that the 978 landmark genes include direct transcriptional targets of the affected pathway and that these change consistently
